Rachel / Marissa —

Working through the questionnaire now. High-level status and notes for the draft deliverable:

- Deliverables: (1) bankwest_bcp_control_matrix.xlsx (control-by-question mapping); (2) SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025.pdf (redacted where needed); (3) rto_rpo_extraction_summary.csv (per-deployment, per-region RTO/RPO); (4) short FAQ about evidence access and on-prem requirements.

- RTO / RPO: For Redwood Hosted (multi-region): typical cold-start RTO for full service failover is 4-6 minutes for active passive failover between us-west and us-east clusters given current cross-region replication of caches; RPO is under 30s for KV/cache and near-zero for persistent logs since we persist tokens to encrypted object store with multi-zone replication. For Dedicated reservations, RTO is customer-configurable — standard SLA-backed config is 2-5 minutes failover when autoscaling between reserved pools is enabled; RPO mirrors hosted for stateful artifacts. For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, RTO/RPO depend on customer networking and latency — we provide guidance and an on-prem runbook.

- Evidence: SOC2 Type II (2025) covers change management, incident response, and access controls; resilience test summaries (chaos exercises and DR failovers) will be included as a high-level appendix. Full test artifacts may require a controlled disclosure process (we can provide redacted summaries or NDA-protected reports).

I'll attach the draft matrix and evidence PDFs for Cyra's review. Rachel, please coordinate any additional commercial ask (credits/SLA exceptions) if BankWest wants tighter RTOs.

—Vivek
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bankwest_bcp_control_matrix.xlsx; SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025.pdf; rto_rpo_extraction_summary.csv
